title: Fundamentals of Generative AI - Week 4 Assignment 4
subject: Fundamentals of Generative AI

questions.question: 1. A VAE is trained on face images. During testing, increasing only z2 changes the person’s smile, head orientation, and lighting simultaneously. What does this observation most strongly indicate?
options: The latent representation is perfectly regularized
The latent representation is entangled
The decoder has ignored Z2
The reconstruction loss has become zero
questions.explanation: When changing a single latent variable alters multiple independent semantic properties simultaneously, the generative factors are entangled.

questions.question: 2. Which observation provides the strongest evidence that a latent representation is disentangled?
options: Every latent variable has a mean exactly equal to zero
The decoder reconstructs every training image perfectly
Changing one latent variable mainly changes one meaningful property while other properties remain nearly unchanged
All latent variables contain equal amounts of information
questions.correctAnswer: Changing one latent variable mainly changes one meaningful property while other properties remain nearly unchanged
questions.explanation: Disentangled representations have an axis-aligned correspondence between individual latent dimensions and real-world ground truth factors of variation.

questions.question: 3. The objective function of a β-VAE is: Suppose β is increased to a very large value. Which outcome is most likely?
options: The encoder can freely store more input-specific information
The approximate posterior is pushed closer to the prior, but reconstruction quality may decrease
The KL-divergence term becomes irrelevant
The model becomes equivalent to a deterministic autoencoder
questions.correctAnswer: The approximate posterior is pushed closer to the prior, but reconstruction quality may decrease
questions.explanation: A very large β heavily prioritizes matching the isotropic Gaussian prior over faithful reconstruction, resulting in a severe information bottleneck that degrades reconstruction sharpness.

questions.question: 4. An image dataset contains six important independent factors of variation, but a β-VAE has only three latent dimensions. Strong disentanglement is enforced. Which result is most reasonable?
options: Each of the six factors will necessarily receive an independent latent dimension
Some latent dimensions will automatically split into additional dimensions
Only some dominant factors may be represented well, while others may be ignored or weakly represented
The reconstruction loss must become exactly zero
questions.correctAnswer: Only some dominant factors may be represented well, while others may be ignored or weakly represented
questions.explanation: Because capacity (3 latent dimensions) is strictly less than generative factors (6), a strongly regularized bottleneck model captures only the top 3 dominant factors of variance.

questions.question: 5. Why can β-annealing be preferable to using a large value of β from the beginning of training?
options: It permanently removes the KL-divergence term
It allows the model to first learn useful reconstruction information and then gradually impose stronger latent regularization
It prevents the decoder from receiving latent variables
It makes the latent variables deterministic throughout training
questions.correctAnswer: It allows the model to first learn useful reconstruction information and then gradually impose stronger latent regularization
questions.explanation: Starting with small β allows the autoencoder to bootstrap meaningful reconstruction representations without collapsing latent codes, before gradually increasing β to enforce disentanglement.

questions.question:
6. For a one-dimensional latent variable:
q_ϕ(z|x) = N(μ, σ²)
and the prior is:
p(z) = N(0, 1)
The KL divergence is calculated as:
DKL = 1/2 [μ² + σ² - log(σ²) - 1]
For: μ = 1 and σ² = 1, what is the KL-divergence value?
questions.explanation: Substituting μ = 1 and σ² = 1 into DKL = 1/2 [μ² + σ² - log(σ²) - 1] yields 1/2 [1² + 1 - log(1) - 1] = 1/2 [1 + 1 - 0 - 1] = 1/2 [1] = 0.5.

questions.question: 7. Which architecture correctly represents a Conditional Variational Autoencoder?
options: Encoder learns q_ϕ(z|x), and decoder learns p_θ(x|z)
Encoder learns q_ϕ(z|x, y), and decoder learns p_θ(x|z, y)
Encoder learns q_ϕ(y|x), and decoder learns p_θ(x|z)
Encoder learns q_ϕ(z|y), and decoder learns p_θ(y|x)
questions.correctAnswer: Encoder learns q_ϕ(z|x, y), and decoder learns p_θ(x|z, y)
questions.explanation: In a Conditional VAE (CVAE), both the inference network (encoder) and the generative network (decoder) are conditioned on the label or attribute vector y.

questions.question: 8. During inference, the same latent vector (z) is supplied twice to a trained CVAE decoder. In the first case, the condition is y=[1, 0], and in the second case, it is y=[0, 1]. What is the most appropriate expectation?
options: The outputs must be identical because (z) is unchanged
The outputs may differ because the decoder uses both (z) and (y)
The second condition is ignored during generation
The latent vector must be sampled again before the condition can affect the output
questions.correctAnswer: The outputs may differ because the decoder uses both (z) and (y)
questions.explanation: Because the decoder generates reconstructions conditioned jointly on latent code z and condition vector y, different conditions y yield different generated outputs even when z is identical.

questions.question:
9. Two input samples have the following latent representations: zA = (2, -1), zB = (-2, 3).
Linear interpolation is performed using: zα = (1 - α)zA + αzB.
What is the interpolated latent vector when α = 0.25?
10. Consider the latent-space interpolation formula: zα = (1 - α)zA + αzB. Which statement is correct?
options: When α = 0, zα = zB, and when α = 1, zα = zA
When α = 0.5, zα is always the zero vector
When α = 0, zα = zA, and when α = 1, zα = zB
Values between 0 and 1 always generate latent points outside the line segment joining zA and zB
questions.correctAnswer: When α = 0, zα = zA, and when α = 1, zα = zB
questions.explanation: At α = 0, (1 - 0)zA + 0·zB = zA. At α = 1, (1 - 1)zA + 1·zB = zB. For α ∈ [0, 1], zα traverses the convex line segment connecting zA to zB.
